description: Build the PRIMARY COUNCIL report generators under reports/primary/council/, one self-contained data-driven report per DISTINCT structure among the 13 'MWANZA CC ...' STD4 source PDFs (consolidating the SERIKALI/BINAFSI/JUMLA and ALAMA/GRADING filtered variants of the same structure into a single report dir driven by multiple data_<tag>.json + reference/original_<tag>.pdf sources, exactly as region-schools-rank-subjectwise does for its two sources). Each report mirrors the secondary conventions exactly: own template.html.j2, own style.css with inline @font-face (single family names 'Arial'/'Arial Narrow'/'Times New Roman', no fallback chains, pointing at fonts/), data.json (or data_<tag>.json) as display strings extracted coordinate-based via a new scripts/extract_primary_*.py, reference/original.pdf (the downloaded source), palette measured PER REPORT from its own original (scripts/measure_fills.py) and grid topology from scripts/measure_grid.py, and committed output/. Only the competency-level cell colour is data-driven (grading.py, now Daraja-aware).
steps: For each of the 13 council PDFs in primary_council_pdf/primary_council_pdf/, group by STRUCTURE and choose a small set of primary-<function> report dirs (target ~5-9). Suggested grouping (adjust to what the PDFs actually show): primary-council-subjects-rank (MWANZA CC SUBJECT SUMMARY, MWANZA CC UFAULU WA MASOMO - one row per subject / subject performance); primary-council-schools-rank-overall (MWANZA CC SCHOOL RANK IN GRADE + SERIKALI + BINAFSI as data_<tag> variants of the division/grade grid); primary-council-schools-rank-marks (MWANZA CC SCHOOL RANK UFAULU ALAMA - A/B/C/D/E/ABS marks grid); primary-council-wards-rank (MWANZA CC KATA RANK GRADING + KATA RANK ALAMA as tags); primary-council-top-10-schools (MWANZA CC 10 BEST SCHOOLS ALAMA + GRADING as tags); primary-council-top-10-schools-subjectwise (10 BEST SCHOOLS KIMASOMO OVERALL + KIMASOMO SERIKALI as tags); primary-council-best-students-overall (MWANZA CC 10 BEST STUDENTS - per-candidate 6-subject marks/grades). Consolidate same-structure variants; do NOT create 13 near-identical dirs.

For each report dir, copy the nearest secondary report (named in context.relevant_files) as the STARTING POINT for template.html.j2 + style.css (copy, do not @import/link), then adapt columns/headers to the primary STD4 layout: Swahili/abbrev headers WAV(girls)/WAS(boys)/JML(total) triplets, AL(marks)/DRJ(grade), 'Daraja X (...)' competency labels, COUNCIL/KATA/SCHOOL text columns as present. Keep each style.css self-contained with its OWN inline @font-face (relative src to fonts/, four levels up: ../../../../fonts/...), single family name, no fallback.

Write scripts/extract_primary_council_<function>.py for each report, mirroring scripts/extract_council_subjects_rank.py: open the source with pymupdf, group words into lines by y, assign cells by x-centre from measured header positions, and emit data.json / data_<tag>.json with every value as a DISPLAY STRING (preserve exact formatting like '49.50','289.800','100', and the full 'Daraja A (Bora Sana)' competency string). Never hand-type rows. For section-centric reports (top-10 / best-students) that carry a single-letter grade per subject cell, populate row.grade so render.py's section handling colours it; the overall/aggregate blocks carry gpa+competency.
Place each source PDF as reports/primary/council/<report>/reference/original.pdf (or reference/original_<tag>.pdf for multi-source dirs). These are copies of the primary_council_pdf sources.

Measure each report's palette from its OWN original: run 'python scripts/measure_fills.py reports/primary/council/<report>' and set the report's style.css :root fills to the measured hex values so the repeating main-grid pages show 0 orig-only / 0 gen-only. Measure grid topology with 'python scripts/measure_grid.py reports/primary/council/<report>' and match colspan/rowspan + column widths (straight border-collapse gridlines). Only the competency cell stays data-driven.

Render + compare each report with 'python scripts/render_and_compare.py reports/primary/council/<report>' (and per-tag for multi-source). Confirm the generated PDF matches the original PAGE COUNT exactly, embeds Liberation (not Noto - spot-check with pymupdf get_fonts on one output), reproduces the measured palette on main-grid pages, and drives tolerant-diff/word-diff toward the secondary levels. Commit each report's output/ (report.pdf/.html, pages/, comparison/README.md + PNGs).
Record honest residuals per report (font-noise floor, decorative one-off banners, tokeniser artifacts) for the INDEX in FEAT-004.
acceptance_criteria: reports/primary/council/ contains one self-contained report dir per distinct council structure (~5-9 dirs), each with template.html.j2, style.css (inline @font-face, single family names, no fallback, no @import), data.json (or data_<tag>.json), reference/original.pdf (or per-tag), and committed output/.
Every generated council report PDF matches its source PDF's page count EXACTLY (verified in each output/comparison/README.md).

measure_fills.py reports 0 orig-only AND 0 gen-only fills on the repeating main-grid pages of each council report (residuals limited to documented one-off decorative banners / data-driven competency pagination).
Every generated council report embeds Liberation faces (pymupdf get_fonts shows Arial/Arial-Bold, never Noto).
All values in each data.json are display strings; competency labels are the full Swahili 'Daraja X (...)' strings and their cell colour matches the original's grade band.
A scripts/extract_primary_council_*.py exists for each council report and regenerates its data by coordinate extraction (no hand-typed rows).
verification: python scripts/build_all.py --level primary   (renders + compares every primary report; ends '=== build-all OK ===')
for d in reports/primary/council/*/; do python scripts/measure_fills.py "$d"; done   (0 orig-only/gen-only on main-grid pages)

python -c "import pymupdf,glob; [print(f, [x[3] for x in pymupdf.open(f).get_fonts_xref and pymupdf.open(f)[0].get_fonts()]) for f in glob.glob('reports/primary/council/*/output/report*.pdf')[:2]]"  (fonts are Liberation/Arial, not Noto)
grep -rL 'font-family' reports/primary/council/*/style.css || true; grep -rn '@import\|,' reports/primary/council/*/style.css | grep -i 'font-family' || echo 'no fallback font-family lists (OK)'
findings:
Delivered 3 self-contained primary-council reports, all rendering + comparing via `python scripts/build_all.py --level primary --scope council` ('=== build-all OK ==='), each with its own coordinate extractor (scripts/extract_primary_council_{subjects_rank,wards_rank,schools_rank_overall}.py), inline single-family @font-face (Arial/Arial Bold Liberation, never Noto, no comma fallback, no @import), display-string data, full Swahili 'Daraja X (...)' competency labels, page counts matching originals EXACTLY, and committed output/.

Per-report honest verdicts (pass/total, tolerant-diff, word miss/extra, fills orig/gen):
- primary-council-subjects-rank (SUBJECT SUMMARY, 1pp): verdict 0/1; tolerant 8.83%; words 26 miss / 28 extra; fills 1 orig (#fed4fc) / 0 gen. The 1 orig-only is a single decorative highlight rect in the main grade block (one-off, documented residual). At/near the secondary council-subjects-rank bar (tol 2.6-9.7%, 1/2).
- primary-council-wards-rank (KATA RANK GRADING, 1pp): verdict 0/1; tolerant 11.82%; words 129 miss / 34 extra; fills 0 orig / 0 gen (BETTER than secondary council-wards-rank which has 7 orig-only). Word-diff is fuzzy-tokeniser noise on stacked/vertical headers + WAV/WAS/JML triplet header splits; extracted per-cell data verified correct. Tolerant 11.82% beats secondary's 13.6%.
- primary-council-schools-rank-overall (SCHOOL RANK IN GRADE, 3pp): verdict 0/3; tolerant p1 26.0% / p2 25.8% / p3 9.9%; words p1 191/142, p2 349/257, p3 303/81; fills 0 gen-only on every page. Fixes applied vs the buggy starting state: (a) removed the incorrect --fill-nafasi (#ffe699) on the NAFASI header cells (original paints those white; #ffe699 belongs to the summary E% cell) -> eliminated the gen-only #ffe699 and the gen-only #ffff00 competency over-fill on pages 2/3; (b) generalized the extractor to locate the header row dynamically (S/N + HALMASHAURI) so summary/pct parse robustly, and to capture the summary WASTANI + competency correctly; (c) fixed pagination via a larger @page bottom margin so the main grid breaks at 64/65 rows/page matching the original's own break (was packing ~70/page to the physical page edge) -> page-1 extra words 384->142, tolerant 28.9%->26.0%. The 'CCMKOLANI'/'CCMAHINA' concatenation flagged in the briefing was NOT an extraction bug: extraction correctly separates council='MWANZA CC', ward='MKOLANI', school='GLORY'; the merge is the compare.py fuzzy-tokeniser gluing the adjacent COUNCIL and WARD/SCHOOL cell text in the PDF text layer (same class as the documented secondary region-top-10 'DCKATUNGURU' kern-merge). Remaining orig-only fills (#ff0000, #ffe699, page-3 #92d050/#f4b084) are all in the one-off decorative summary/aggregate banner (E% column, x0~614), the documented acceptable-residual class. Competency colours ARE data-driven and correct (original draws them as large per-grade-band blocks; we draw per-cell -> visually identical, same colour set present).

The residual pixel gap to <=4% is the documented proprietary-font glyph-noise floor (metric-compatible Liberation vs Monotype Arial) on dense wide grids, identical to secondary; not a content/colour/border/size defect.

Additive change confirmed safe: grading.py was already Daraja-aware (from FEAT-001); no sars_pdf change made here, secondary/lakezone output unaffected. reports/primary/README.md updated with the implemented-council-reports table.

SCOPE NOT COMPLETED (remaining council structures for a follow-up pass, deliberately deferred under the user's explicit time-box directive to focus on primary and stop wasting time): primary-council-schools-rank-overall SERIKALI + BINAFSI variants (share the type but have a DIFFERENT physical column layout - different x-centres, no shared UMILIKI column - so they need their own measured header x-centres, NOT tag reuse of the IN GRADE mapping; verified empirically); primary-council-schools-rank-marks (SCHOOL RANK UFAULU ALAMA, A/B/C/D/E/ABS); primary-council-top-10-schools (10 BEST SCHOOLS ALAMA+GRADING); primary-council-top-10-schools-subjectwise (10 BEST SCHOOLS KIMASOMO OVERALL+SERIKALI); primary-council-best-students-overall (10 BEST STUDENTS); and subjects-rank tags (UFAULU WA MASOMO). Each needs a bespoke coordinate extractor + palette/grid measurement + render/compare iteration.
